subject: Taxes
title: Jewish Tax Revolts
description: Learn Jewish Tax Revolts in one minute.

hook.text: In 66 CE, Jews revolted against Rome partly over crushing taxes.

buildup.text: Rome taxed Judea through local collaborators. The high priests collected taxes for Rome, earning fierce resentment.

discovery.text: Zealots—radical anti-tax rebels—assassinated tax collaborators in broad daylight. Tax resistance became holy war.

twist.text: After crushing the revolt, Rome imposed the Fiscus Judaicus: a special tax on all Jews throughout the empire.

climax.text: The Jewish revolts show how taxes intertwine with identity, religion, and freedom. Tax isn't just fiscal—it's political.

punchline.text: A tax revolt became a holy war. Rome destroyed the Temple.

quiz.question: What was the Fiscus Judaicus?
options: A special tax imposed on all Jews after the revolt
